BLOCKER: Gate never fails on non-grandfathered placeholder completions: `audit()` results are appended only to `warnings`, so items outside the baseline still exit 0 — AC requires failing "unless grandfathered".

Diff contains no wiring into precheck fast or ci-cd-gates.json, and no RCCA/annotation updates to BI-PF-1409 or BI-PF-1294 (links.reopened_by/decision note) — AC bullets 1, 4 and 5 are absent from this change.
`--self-test` does not cover a baseline scenario (AC requires placeholder, RCCA, baseline, clean); only 4 scenarios run and baseline is untested in it.
MAJOR: Fail-open design: if `merge-base develop` and `origin/develop` both fail, `_git` swallows the error and `transitions()` returns [] → gate exits 0 with no indication it checked nothing.
`PF_ALLOW_PLACEHOLDER_DOD=1` env bypass is not in the AC and downgrades failures without an explicit "escape hatch used" marker in output, enabling silent CI disablement.
Baseline is never reconciled with real data: stale/duplicate/already-remediated IDs are undetected, so the "drive to zero" count can drift or be gamed indefinitely.
`remaining` count is warning-only and unbounded by baseline health: after `until` expires the 87 items become non-baselined but still only warn.
MINOR: Docstring promises "one JSON line on stderr"; `_emit` prints JSON plus human lines to stdout — contract mismatch for downstream parsers.
`audit()` silently `continue`s on unparseable item files, hiding corruption from observability.
Audit output reports only a count, not the offending item IDs, weakening actionability.
`--self-test` falls through and executes the full gate afterward instead of exiting after the matrix.
`transitions()` uses `--name-only` (no `-M`/`--name-status`), so renames of already-completed items can be misread as new completions.
`_exists()` does `ROOT / p` plus `ROOT.glob(p)` on data-supplied strings — accepts `..`/glob patterns, an existence oracle in gate output.
NIT: `MIN_FIELD` is enforced only for rcca fields; a 1–2 character AC/verification entry passes as "specific".
`origin/develop` hardcoded fallback alongside merge-base duplicates ref policy in code.
store-registry entry sets `owner` to a script path rather than an accountable owner/team.
SUMMARY: The gate logic is a reasonable tooling-Python addition and tests exist, but as delivered it cannot fail a bad completion outside the grandfathered list, lacks required wiring and item-level RCCA/re-open evidence, and is fail-open on git resolution errors.
Top risks: false confidence from a green gate, permanent baseline ratchet with no reconciliation, and self-test/AC coverage gaps hiding regressions.
